{{short description|American mathematician (born 1938)}}
'''Peter Paul Nikolas Orlik''' (born 12 November 1938, in [[Budapest]])<ref>biographical information from ''American Men and Women of Science'', Thomson Gale 2004</ref> is an American mathematician, known for his research on [[topology]], algebra, and [[combinatorics]].<ref name=2008Conference>[http://www.fields.utoronto.ca/programs/scientific/08-09/orlik-conf/ Conference in honour of Peter Orlik, Fields Institute, August 2008]</ref>

Orlik earned in 1961 his bachelor's degree from the [[Norwegian Institute of Technology]] in [[Trondheim]] and in 1966 his Ph.D. from the [[University of Michigan]] under [[Frank Raymond (mathematician)|Frank Raymond]] with thesis ''Necessary conditions for the homeomorphism of Seifert manifolds''.<ref>{{MathGenealogyProject|id=5509}}</ref> He became in 1966 an assistant professor and in 1973 a full professor at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]].

Orlik was in the academic year 1971/72 a visiting professor in [[Oslo]]. From 1967 to 1969 he was a visiting scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref>[http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/scholars?lastname=orlik&firstname=&schools=All&years=&types= Institute for Advanced Study: A Community of Scholars]</ref>

Orlik is the author of over 70 publications. He works on [[Seifert manifold]]s, [[singularity theory]], [[braid theory]], [[reflection group]]s, [[invariant theory]], and hypergeometric integrals.<ref name=2008Conference/> He was, with [[Louis Solomon]] and [[Hiroaki Terao]], a pioneer of the theory of [[arrangements of hyperplanes]] in complex space.

In 2012 he was elected a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]</ref>
